newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin under fire over daughter's Kremlin job.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin under fire over daughter's Kremlin job.

text.p: The head of the State Duma, Russia's lower house of parliament, accused President Boris Yeltsin of illegal nepotism on Tuesday for appointing his own daughter as his official Kremlin image-maker.

Gennady Seleznyov told reporters Monday's decree naming 37-year-old Tatyana Dyachenko adviser to the president contradicted the law on Russia's civil service, a bill approved by parliament and by the president himself.
"Lamentably, it is the second time the president infringed the Civil Service Law," Seleznyov said. "There is a restriction there on sons, daughters or other relatives, but the president ignored it."

Seleznyov alleged the first time the law was broken was when Yeltsin appointed businessman Boris Berezovsky as deputy secretary of the powerful Security Council last October. His objection on that occasion was that Berezovsky has Israeli as well as Russian citizenship.
Dyachenko's appointment had been long expected. She succesfully advised Yeltsin during his re-election campaign last year and has since become increasingly influential in Kremlin circles.
